methodology.description: Public draft-helper PPR redraft board. Player value and market cost are intentionally kept separate. Rankings blend broad expert consensus, current projections, recent independent expert boards and material preseason/news context; ADP is treated as price rather than player quality. League scoring, roster construction, draft slot, drafted players, positional scarcity and next-pick pressure are applied by the client recommendation engine.
rankingInputs: FantasyPros 2026 PPR consensus cheat sheet (36 experts) and most-accurate-expert board checked Aug. 29
ESPN Field Yates PPR Top 160 updated Aug. 28 plus Aug. 29 NFL/fantasy news
RotoWire PPR cheat sheet updated Aug. 29, including current expert dispersion and injury flags
CBS Sports current PPR ADP/model coverage and injury reporting through Aug. 29
NFL.com preseason Week 3, depth-chart and player-news reporting through Aug. 29
methodology.marketInput: Current PPR ADP remains a separate market-price input, cross-checked across FantasyPros, CBS and RotoWire. ADP is not used as a substitute for player value; large gaps are preserved when news risk or expert disagreement justifies them.
newsInputs: De'Von Achane moves materially upward after the prior board proved too conservative relative to current PPR expert value. ESPN has him No. 8 overall, FantasyPros' most-accurate-expert sample has him No. 15, and the broader FantasyPros PPR consensus has him No. 20; CBS PPR ADP remains around the end of Round 1. The new rank deliberately sits between those views rather than blindly following market price.

Derrick Henry moves materially upward. ESPN ranks him No. 11, FantasyPros' most-accurate-expert sample No. 24, and CBS PPR ADP is roughly 13. The prior No. 28 rank was too bearish relative to the current independent range.

Ashton Jeanty moves down after remaining questionable with an ankle injury and after Raiders coach Klint Kubiak publicly discussed excitement about a possible two-back structure with rookie Mike Washington Jr. The market still prices Jeanty much more aggressively, so the value-vs-ADP gap is intentionally preserved.

Puka Nacua remains elite but confidence falls again after he was listed questionable with a groin issue on Aug. 28, on top of unresolved discipline uncertainty. RotoWire still ranks him No. 4 and FantasyPros consensus No. 3, so the injury changes risk more than baseline talent value.

Christian McCaffrey moves slightly up as current expert boards continue to place him well above the prior No. 9 slot despite the lingering questionable tag. The injury discount remains embedded in confidence and expert range.
No other Aug. 29 injury, suspension, trade, depth-chart or preseason development justified a larger top-30 move in the public board.
methodology.notes: Expert disagreement is preserved with expertHigh/expertLow ranges; unresolved injuries, discipline risk and genuine model disagreement can intentionally widen those ranges. Confidence reflects agreement plus news certainty, not ceiling. This file is used only by smhillis/sleeper-draft-helper-public and must not be copied into or used to modify Scott's personal Sleeper Draft Assistant.

players.name: Puka Nacua
players.news: Still an elite PPR value, but confidence drops after an Aug. 28 groin designation was added to the unresolved discipline risk. Current independent boards still place him roughly No. 3-5 overall, so the baseline rank holds while the downside range stays wide.

players.name: Christian McCaffrey
players.news: Moves up modestly because ESPN, RotoWire and the most-accurate FantasyPros sample continue to value him above the prior No. 9 slot. The lingering questionable tag still keeps confidence below the other first-round anchors.

players.name: James Cook III
players.news: Current independent boards cluster around RB5-RB6/top-13 overall, while some model-driven work remains more bearish. The public rank moves closer to the current human-expert center without erasing that disagreement.

players.name: A.J. Brown
players.news: Broad PPR consensus still supports an early-second-round value, but ESPN is materially lower. The wider expert range is preserved rather than forcing a false consensus.

players.name: De'Von Achane
players.news: Major upward correction from No. 23. ESPN ranks him No. 8, FantasyPros' most-accurate-expert sample No. 15 and broader PPR consensus No. 20. The new value rank sits near the middle of that unusually wide range while keeping ADP separate.

players.name: Nico Collins
players.news: FantasyPros remains much higher than ESPN, producing one of the widest top-30 disagreements. Rank stays in the mid-second-round value area but confidence is reduced.

players.name: Chris Olave
players.news: Target-volume outlook remains strong; current FantasyPros PPR consensus still places him in the mid-to-late second-round value tier.

players.name: Omarion Hampton
players.news: Broad breakout support remains intact. Current expert value and market cost are close enough that no artificial value premium is added.

players.name: Kenneth Walker III
players.news: Current expert boards still support top-24 overall value, but the recent ankle swelling keeps the downside range wide.

players.name: Derrick Henry
players.news: Major upward correction from No. 28. ESPN has Henry No. 11 overall, CBS PPR ADP is roughly 13 and FantasyPros' most-accurate-expert sample has him No. 24. The public value rank now reflects that spread instead of anchoring to the bearish edge.

players.name: Rashee Rice
players.news: No additional NFL discipline remains the key positive; knee recovery is still the principal uncertainty. ESPN remains aggressive while broader consensus is more cautious.

players.name: Malik Nabers
players.news: Still trending toward Week 1 following ACL recovery, but the injury tag remains. Current expert boards broadly place him in the 20s, so the rank stays conservative without assuming a setback.

players.name: Ashton Jeanty
players.news: Moves down from No. 21. He remains questionable with the ankle injury, and Klint Kubiak has now publicly discussed excitement about a two-back structure involving Mike Washington Jr. Market price remains much richer than the risk-adjusted player-value rank.
